name: Charlotte
lede: The disc golf capital of the South — more championship courses per capita than anywhere. Charlotte's five published courses are all free and all seriously good.
introParagraphs: Charlotte is the best disc golf city in the South, period. Hornets Nest is the famous one — open front nine, wooded Piedmont back nine, and a tournament history that includes the national championship. Nevin Park's Nightmare layout is the long, brutal sibling, and Kilborne, Reedy Creek, and The Scrapyard round out a top tier most metros would kill for.

All five of our published courses are free, and the variety is the point: open parkland, dense Piedmont woods, water carries, and one 1,001-foot par 5 (well, that one's across the border in Kentucky).
New here? Start at Kilborne, then face the Nightmare once you're feeling bold.

faqs.question: How many disc golf courses are in the Charlotte metro?
faqs.answer: Around 50 courses across the metro including the South Carolina side. We're publishing the best first — 5 are live today, with more added every week.

faqs.question: What's the best disc golf course in Charlotte?
faqs.answer: Hornets Nest is the most famous and most-loved — an open front nine and a wooded Piedmont back nine with tournament history. Nevin Park's Nightmare layout is the serious challenger.

faqs.question: Are Charlotte's disc golf courses free?
faqs.answer: Yes — all five of our published courses (Hornets Nest, Kilborne, Reedy Creek, The Scrapyard, Nevin Nightmare) are free to play.

faqs.question: What's the best beginner course in Charlotte?
faqs.answer: Kilborne TPC is the friendliest of the published five — flat, well-maintained, and fair. Work up to Reedy Creek and The Scrapyard as your lines improve.
